text.p: German engineering and defence group Rheinmetall AG said on Tuesday it had doubled its stake in auto components maker Kolbenschmidt AG to 53.5 percent.

The company said in a statment it bought another 28.5 percent of Kolbenschmidt shares from financial investors. It had previously bought 25.3 percent of Kolbenschmidt from Commerzbank and on the stock exchange.

Rheinmetall said the acquisition made good on repeated statements that it intended to integrate Kolbenschmidt into its business. Kolbenschmidt's sales and earnings will be consolidated into Rheinmetall's group results this year.

An extraordinary shareholders meeting will be held this year to clear the takeover, after which Rheinmetall will probably own over 75 percent of a merged unit made up of Kolbenschmidt and its own Pierburg AG unit, the company said.
Rheinmetall said the acquisition, which has already been approved by the German cartel office, would help it to build automotive components into its largest business area by sales.
Kolbenschmidt and Pierburg together employ over 10,000 worker and have combined sales of 2.3 billion marks.
